elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such rights to Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation"
"Vendor's retained rights in Vendor Technology are governed by Section 14.3"; Vendor Technology = "Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates..."

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: Redline contains no embedded-IP licence grant; it only cross-references "Section 14.3" for Vendor's retained rights, and the official check records the embedded-IP licence as limited to "named technology categories"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: No Customer Data language in the redlined clause; only "Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data" in the definition

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how" plus "retained rights in Vendor Technology are governed by Section 14.3"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in deliverables
elements.evidence: Redline grants no licence to Customer at all; the original "revocable, non-transferable licence ... only during the applicable Order Form term" was deleted

elements.element: Licence permits use, modification and sublicensing for Customer's business
elements.evidence: No use/modify/sublicense language appears in the rendered clause

offending_extra_words: Vendor's retained rights in Vendor Technology are governed by Section 14.3.
all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation
reasons: Ownership flip and assignment are achieved, but the preferred level also requires an express perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in the Deliverables; the redline only cross-references Section 14.3 for Vendor's retained rights and the official check confirms the existing grant is limited to named technology categories rather than any embedded Vendor IP.
Customer Data rights are not addressed in the operative text; nothing in the redline confirms Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
Fallback is independently unmet: the redline deletes the licence sentence and grants no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.

Minimality fails: the edit expands 25 words to 39 (ratio 1.56) and changes 73% of characters; the added cross-reference sentence about Vendor Technology is unnecessary duplication since Section 14.3 already governs, and the ownership flip could be achieved with a tighter operator-level edit plus a short assignment insertion.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced and the surrounding commercial terms remain effective.
